old_problem: The prior record correctly rejected the all-four-protocol assumption, but treated the platform-configured slot count and project-selected matrix as a permanent semantic decision rather than parameterizable readiness data.
disposition_reason: `Multiple` establishes at least two concurrent, differently sourced images; `such as` makes the listed protocols and OS installation examples rather than a mandatory four-protocol/destructive matrix. The Project SPEC binds two or more supported methods, images and configured slots. Independent read of a unique marker from every mounted image proves it can be operated on without booting or installing.
decision_basis: XLSX row 748, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2 and historical record were directly examined.
OpenBMC's design explicitly supports multiple simultaneous connections and states that the available count is configuration-defined; it also exposes distinct configured VirtualMedia members.
The generic design documents Proxy plus CIFS/HTTPS Legacy paths, so HTTP/NFS may be used only when the actual OEM capability/SOP proves them.
ED-35 prevents claiming install coverage, while ED-36 allows the exact count/matrix and endpoint data to remain Project Configuration.

test_case.test_name: Verify concurrent, independently attributable virtual-media images up to the approved matrix
test_case.purpose: Demonstrate that at least two project-supported virtual-media methods can keep distinct approved images mounted simultaneously, each image remains independently readable and correctly mapped, and all sessions can be removed without stale devices or host/BMC degradation.
required_package: BMC firmware configuration or vendor evidence listing available VirtualMedia slots and per-slot mode/protocol support
Approved matrix N >= 2 with one endpoint, protocol, immutable image hash and unique read-only marker per slot
Actual WebUI/Remote Console procedure and protocol-specific trust/credential policies
Isolated SUT, complete boot/storage/USB baseline and independent recovery console
test_case.test_command: Enumerate configured virtual-media members/slots and confirm the approved N does not exceed them. Operator mounts the matrix one image at a time in the actual WebUI, preserving visual status after each step. After every insertion, correlate the exact slot and immutable image with a new host optical/USB device and read only its unique marker. Once all N coexist, re-read every marker while all sessions remain active. Eject in reverse approved order and verify each corresponding device disappears. Do not boot or install.
test_case.expected_result: All N approved images are simultaneously active in distinct supported slots; every image-to-protocol-to-device mapping is unambiguous; each unique marker is readable while the full set is mounted; no slot, image or content crosses mappings; reverse cleanup removes every session/device and leaves no boot/storage/BMC health change.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires N >= 2, configuration-supported capacity, per-image hash/marker identity, per-step visual and device correlation, simultaneous independent reads, and complete ordered cleanup. FAIL includes slot exhaustion below approved capacity, partial/stale mount, wrong mapping/content, one image disrupting another, unexpected write/boot, or incomplete eject. Unsupported methods are N/A only with authoritative Project SPEC and cannot be reported as tested.
safety_gate: Never assume all four named methods are supported; bind only documented platform methods and slots
Validate every endpoint, certificate/security policy and hash; do not expose credentials
Use read-only images/markers; do not change boot order, launch installers or write host disks
Stop on ambiguous device attribution, resource exhaustion, console loss or partial failure and do not automatically retry
Record and verify reverse-order cleanup of every session
expected_evidence: BMC model/firmware and configured slot/member inventory
Approved N-slot method/image matrix with redacted endpoint security and hashes
Per-insertion WebUI screenshots, device/USB mapping and unique-marker read results
All-concurrent re-read results, resource/health logs and per-eject disappearance through zero active media
test_case.recovery: On partial mount or misattribution, stop adding media, preserve the full slot/device map, and eject only according to the documented cleanup order. If a medium cannot be removed or console health degrades, use the independent recovery path and escalate before reboot or retry; never resolve by booting an image.

source_conflict.preserved_original_conflict: The Master leaves count, selected examples and the meaning of `operations` open.
source_conflict.resolution: N is configuration-bound with N >= 2, methods come from the supported project matrix, and a non-destructive unique-marker read supplies the observable operation without claiming installation.

blocked.reason: The core concurrent operation and PASS oracle are defined; capacity and matrix are runtime/project bindings.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Configured slot capacity, supported methods, N-slot endpoints/images/security, unique markers and cleanup order.
